cita: Gaurav et al. (2025). CodeMem: Architecting Reproducible Agents via Dynamic MCP and Procedural Memory.
problema: Vanilla CodeAct agents suffer probabilistic instability, redundant re-derivation of already-solved logic, inability to retain user feedback across sessions, and context drift during long multi-step workflows, making them unreliable for repetitive real-world tasks.
mecanismo: CodeMem couples Dynamic-MCP tool discovery (search_functions/load_functions, JIT schema loading) with a Python sandbox (execute_code) and a procedural-memory bank: validated Python functions are frozen via register_skill after a trial-and-confirm phase, letting future sessions execute (Texecute) instead of re-plan/re-write/re-debug; write_todos externalizes plan state as an anchor against context truncation.
evaluacion: LLM-as-judge (Gemini 2.5 Flash) scores full agent trajectories (tool calls, sandbox code, stdout/stderr, side-effects) over a curated dataset of 25 multi-step agentic tasks (difficulty 1-5, 2-8 chained tools) across three backbone models.
numeros_clave: Table 2: Gemini 3 Full 96% min correctness / 7.00 avg calls / 100.48s P50 latency / 2.02M tokens; Claude 4.5 Sonnet 79% / 6.96 calls / 71.38s / 2.61M tokens; GPT-5 Chat 68% / 2.80 calls / 14.75s / 0.49M tokens.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: write_todos externalizes a Pending->In-Progress->Completed checklist outside the chat history so the agent recovers exact plan position after a sandbox crash or context truncation (SS5.4/SS6.5) -- a concrete pattern for MF's plan-state memory.

register_skill freezes a validated Python function into a permanent library only after an explicit trial+user-confirmation phase (SS5.2), a discretionary promotion trigger MF's CONSOLIDACION could adopt.

SS3.3 and Table 2 show standard tool-calling context grows O(N) with steps while CodeMem stays O(1) (data stays in sandbox RAM, not the LLM context), and reuse collapses Ttask to ~Texecute -- supports MF's context-economy thesis.

notes: Table 2 (SS7.3) anchors the quantitative claims; Fig.2 diagrams the architecture; case study in SS6 (Outlook-OneDrive) grounds register_skill/write_todos mechanics.

cita: Li et al. (2026). Experience-Evolving Multi-Turn Tool-Use Agent with Hybrid Episodic-Procedural Memory.
problema: Multi-turn tool-use agents face shifting decision contexts where full-trajectory reuse is too context-specific to transfer and tool-only graphs ignore dialogue/environment context, leaving experience reuse either coarse-grained or context-blind.
mecanismo: H-EPM builds a state-annotated tool-transition graph from accumulated trajectories: edges encode procedural transition weights (frequency + efficiency) and attach episodic summarized-state annotations (via an autonomous state-summarization tool) between tool nodes; at inference the agent adaptively chooses episodic recall (state-summary similarity) vs. procedural exploitation (edge weight) for next-tool selection, and the same graph biases RL rollout exploration toward historically successful tool transitions (memory-guided GRPO).
evaluacion: Inference-time evaluation on 4 multi-turn tool-use benchmarks (tau-Bench Telecom, tau2-Bench Retail, ToolSandbox, ACEBench) against retrieval, ReasoningBank, and tool-graph baselines across multiple backbones (GPT-4.1, GPT-4.1-mini, GPT-4o, Qwen3); RL evaluation integrates H-EPM into GRPO rollout vs. base GRPO and AgentEvolver on tau-Bench Retail (Qwen3-4B-Instruct).
numeros_clave: Abstract: up to 50%+ inference-time gains over baselines and up to 40%+ improvement on out-of-distribution RL tasks; gains reported as more pronounced for weaker backbones (GPT-4.1-mini benefits more than GPT-4.1/GPT-4o).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The POMDP formulation tracks interaction history h_t and compact state summaries s_t across turns (SS3-4.1) as decision context, not an explicit plan/task-state artifact -- relevant context but no direct MF-style plan-state memory design.

Edge weights blend transition frequency with an efficiency term w'(tau_t,tau_t+1) (SS4.2) that continuously reweights procedural routines by successful trajectories, offering a graph-based consolidation mechanism MF could adapt for promoting recurring gotchas to durable recipes.

Efficiency-aware edge weighting (SS4.2) explicitly penalizes tool overuse by rollout-step count, aligning with MF's context-economy concern that recall must weigh cost/latency, not just semantic similarity.

notes: Table 1 reports per-benchmark/per-backbone inference gains; Table 3 reports RL gains vs GRPO/AgentEvolver; Fig.1-2 diagram graph construction and adaptive retrieval (SS4.2-4.3).

cita: Liu et al. (2025). Unifying Dynamic Tool Creation and Cross-Task Experience Sharing through Cognitive Memory Architecture.
problema: LLM agents struggle to adapt to novel tasks because tool-creation approaches build tools from scratch without reusing past experience, while experience-sharing approaches transfer trajectories but lack integrated tool creation -- fragmenting adaptive, cumulative learning.
mecanismo: SMITH organizes memory into procedural (Mproc, static system prompts/behavior), semantic (Msem, human-crafted tool examples/demonstrations) and episodic (Mep, embedded successful trajectories) components; tool creation is an iterative sandboxed code-generation loop until success feedback, and cross-task reuse retrieves top-k semantically-similar episodic/semantic experiences via dense-sparse hybrid retrieval (text-embedding-3-large + Splade, RRF fusion) to condition the next action; a curriculum-learning module reranks tasks via an ensemble of proxy agents' difficulty re-estimation.
evaluacion: GAIA benchmark (165 validation tasks, levels 1-3) with a multi-agent planner/developer-tester workflow, 3-path sampling with LLM-as-a-judge (o4-mini) consensus voting, compared against tool-creation (Alita) and experience-sharing (Memento) SOTA baselines, plus ablations removing curriculum learning, episodic memory sharing, and cold-start demonstrations.
numeros_clave: 81.8% Pass@1 on GAIA (vs Alita 75.2%, Memento 70.9%); ablation Table 3: -10.3% w/o curriculum learning, -13.9% w/o episodic memory sharing, -21.8% w/o cold-start demonstrations.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: plan_estado=SI per extraction, but SMITH's planner/developer-tester loop (SS4, Fig.1) tracks sub-plan execution implicitly through the outer loop rather than an explicit persisted plan-state object -- adjacent but not a direct plan-state memory design.

Ablation Table 3 measures episodic memory sharing contributing +13.9% and cold-start demonstrations +21.8%, empirically confirming that consolidating and reusing prior successful trajectories/tools materially improves task success -- supports MF's consolidation thesis.

SMITH's tri-partite Mproc/Msem/Mep hierarchy (SS3.3, Eq.7-8) keeps each memory type in a distinct store retrieved through one consistent interface, illustrating a multi-store-with-single-retrieval-seam design relevant to MF's COSTURAS question.

notes: Table 1 (GAIA main results) and Table 3 (ablation) anchor the numbers; Fig.4 shows the temporal shift from semantic to episodic memory reliance across curriculum progression.

cita: OPPO AI Agent Team, LV-NUS lab (2025). MemEvolve: Meta-Evolution of Agent Memory Systems.
problema: Self-evolving agent memory systems rely on manually engineered, static architectures: while agents can accumulate experience within a fixed memory pipeline, the memory architecture itself cannot meta-adapt to diverse task domains, leaving performance misaligned whenever a task's memory affordances differ.
mecanismo: MemEvolve runs a bilevel (dual) evolution: an inner loop lets the agent populate an empty memory under a fixed candidate architecture Omega=(Encode,Store,Retrieve,Manage) across a batch of trajectories; an outer loop's diagnose-and-design meta-evolution operator F Pareto-ranks candidates on (performance,-cost,-delay), selects top-K parents, diagnoses architectural bottlenecks per component from trajectory replay, and generates new (E,U,R,G) variants -- grounded on EvolveLab, a modular codebase re-implementing 12 prior memory systems (Voyager, ExpeL, AWM, G-Memory, Memp, etc.) under one interface.
evaluacion: Evaluated on four agentic benchmarks (GAIA, WebWalkerQA, xBench-DeepSearch, TaskCraft) atop frameworks SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher, comparing MemEvolve-evolved architectures against the 12 EvolveLab baselines and testing cross-benchmark/cross-LLM transfer of memory architectures evolved on TaskCraft.
numeros_clave: Improves frameworks such as SmolAgent and Flash-Searcher by up to 17.06%; memory architectures evolved on TaskCraft show 2.0-9.09% gains when transferred to unseen benchmarks/backbones (abstract); Table 2 lists per-benchmark Pass@1 across 20+ agent frameworks (e.g., Flash-Searcher GPT-5-mini 81.18% GAIA avg.).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: The Manage(G) component explicitly performs consolidation/abstraction/forgetting (SS3.2) and is itself meta-evolved by diagnose-and-design (SS4.2) -- a self-improving consolidation policy MF's CONSOLIDACION anchor could draw from.

The outer-loop fitness vector explicitly includes token cost and latency alongside task performance (Fj=(Perf,-Cost,-Delay), SS4.1) and Pareto-ranks candidates on this tradeoff, directly confirming MF's context-economy framing of memory design.

EvolveLab's modular (Encode,Store,Retrieve,Manage) decomposition (Table1, SS3.2) treats the retrieval index/store as a swappable, evolvable derived layer rather than fixed ground truth, echoing MF's Tier-3 derived-index-as-cache framing.

notes: Table 2 (main cross-framework/cross-benchmark results) and Table 1 (12 EvolveLab baselines taxonomy) anchor the numbers; Fig.3 diagrams the dual inner/outer evolutionary loop (SS4.1-4.2).

cita: Gaurav et al. (2025). Synthesizing Procedural Memory: Challenges and Architectures in Automated Workflow Generation.
problema: The mechanism for autonomously synthesizing procedural memory 'from a blank slate' is underexplored: agents must transition from passive tool-users to active workflow architects, but four structural bottlenecks -- Discovery, Verification, Decomposition, Scaling -- block reliable automated skill generation.
mecanismo: The paper proposes: (1) Dynamic MCP search/load_functions for O(1) tool discovery instead of O(N) prompt injection; (2) a 'Probe' methodology -- sample with strict pagination, print raw structure to stdout, then lock the schema -- to avoid hallucinated data shapes before writing final code; (3) Linear State Anchoring via write_todos as an external program-counter, replacing search-tree decomposition (LATS) for linear workflows with intrinsic LLM reasoning; (4) production-hardening via asyncio concurrency and external persistence (SQLite/Sheets checkpoints) plus idempotent operations for scaling.
evaluacion: Single high-fidelity qualitative case study (Outlook-to-OneDrive cross-service orchestration workflow) with an illustrative HumanEval/83 comparison contrasting a LATS/GPT-4 'reflection trap' against modern intrinsic-reasoning (GPT-5) derivation; no formal quantitative benchmark table.
numeros_clave: Illustrative, not benchmarked: naive sequential processing of 1000 emails ~33 minutes vs. concurrent asyncio.gather ~2 minutes (SS5.1); case study probe reports 'Fetched 7 emails with attachments' as schema-locking evidence (SS3.3).

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: write_todos as 'Linear State Anchoring' (SS4.3) is explicitly proposed as an external Program Counter surviving context flush/truncation, directly extending MF's plan-state-as-memory need (P13) with a concrete decouple-plan-from-context pattern.

The 'Probe' methodology (SS3, sample->inspect stdout->codify) is a structural anti-hallucination discipline that grounds tool-response schemas in observed reality before code generation, a concrete pattern for MF's FIDELIDAD anchor (grounding/provenance against poisoning by invented structure).

SS2.1/2.4 quantify tool-schema injection as O(N) context cost vs. O(1) retrieval-based discovery, and SS5.1 shows async concurrency dropping a 1000-email workflow from ~33min to ~2min -- both confirm MF's context/latency economy framing.

notes: Case study spans SS2-5 (Outlook/OneDrive running example, companion to CodeMem W4417531516); Fig.1 (HumanEval/83 comparison) is the only figure with concrete numbers; evidencia_tipo=CUALITATIVA confirmed -- no formal benchmark table found in the PDF.

cita: Zhang et al. (2026). MemRL: Self-Evolving Agents via Runtime Reinforcement Learning on Episodic Memory.
problema: Current memory-based agents rely on passive semantic-similarity retrieval that cannot distinguish high-utility experiences from noisy-but-similar ones, while fine-tuning the backbone to internalize experience is costly and prone to catastrophic forgetting -- leaving no tuning-free way to exploit runtime feedback for retrieval quality.
mecanismo: MemRL structures episodic memory as Intent-Experience-Utility triplets and formalizes retrieval as a value-based decision process (Memory-MDP): a Two-Phase Retrieval first recalls a semantically-similar candidate pool via cosine similarity/threshold, then re-ranks by a composite score blending normalized similarity and a learned Q-value; Q-values are updated online via a Monte-Carlo/TD rule from environmental reward (success/failure), while the backbone LLM stays frozen -- learning happens entirely in the retrieval policy over memory, not in model weights.
evaluacion: Runtime-learning and transfer evaluations on four benchmarks (HLE, BigCodeBench, ALFWorld, LifelongAgentBench OS/DB) against RAG, Self-RAG, Mem0 and MemP baselines under a frozen-backbone setting, reporting Success Rate and Cumulative Success Rate over 10 epochs, plus ablations on the Q-weighting factor lambda and cross-task vs single-task retrieval scope.
numeros_clave: Runtime learning: MemRL beats strongest baseline MemP by +3.8% avg CSR (up to +6.2% on ALFWorld/OS); Transfer: +2.8% avg SR (+5.8% ALFWorld); ablation shows lambda=0.5 is optimal Q-weighting (Fig.5); cross-task retrieval beats single-task Reflexion-style baseline on OS (+9.0%) and ALFWorld (+5.1%), Table 3.

mf_aplicabilidad.nota: MemRL empirically shows pure cosine-similarity retrieval (lambda=0) plateaus and retrieves 'functional distractors' (SS5.3.2 ablation), while augmenting with a learned utility (Q-value) signal from environmental feedback yields robust gains -- confirms MF's G-M2 stance that retrieval must be MEASURED (grounded in outcome-based signal), not semantic similarity alone.

MemRL optimizes retrieval policy without weight updates to avoid fine-tuning compute cost (SS1), but reports no explicit token/latency accounting for the memory itself -- relevant context for MF's context-economy thesis without direct confirmation/refutation.

Utility (Q-value) updates via Monte-Carlo/TD rules (Eq.3-4, SS4.3) continuously reweight which stored experiences are worth reusing based on environmental feedback, offering a quantitative consolidation mechanism (vs. MF's qualitative gotcha-to-recipe promotion) worth considering for CONSOLIDACION.

notes: Table 1 (runtime) and Table 2 (transfer) anchor the CSR/SR numbers; Fig.5 shows the lambda ablation; Table 3 isolates cross-task vs single-task retrieval scope (SS5.3.3).
